title: A request reads its memory as three numbers on `Core\Budget`, and the runtime records the peak rather than waiting to be asked
scope:
where a request's memory figures live, what they are called, and how the high-water mark
reaches an operator who never wrote a line to ask for it. Not in scope: what the counter measures,
which [0005](0005.md) settled and
`crates/nvs-runtime/src/budget.rs` implements; whether a memory budget is per request or per
isolate tree, which is `rule:security/isolate-budget-is-the-trees`' to
settle and which this inherits rather than decides; and the `Core\Net` socket surface, which is the
one ADR loop goal `net-os-signal` was already authorised to open.
dependsOnText:
[0005](0005.md), whose `[limits] memory` is the ceiling all
three numbers are read against; [0051](0051.md), whose roster placed the
figure on `Core\Os`; [0076](0076.md), whose default series this adds a tenth
row to; [0127](0127.md), whose `Script\ExitReport` gains a fourth accessor;
and [0067](0067.md), whose `slow_query` threshold is the shape the warning
copies rather than reinvents.
validatedBy:
`crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/migration-members-outstanding.txt`, whose keys move from
`Core\Os::memoryUsage` to the three on `Core\Budget` and stay owed until loop goal `net-os-signal` strikes them;
and `benches/abi-probe`, which is where the claim that the high-water update is free has to survive
measurement rather than assertion.

summary.headline: A request reads its memory as three numbers, and the peak is always recorded
summary.body:
`Core\Budget::memoryHeld`, `memoryPeak` and `memoryLimit` are the three numbers a request can
ask about itself; the process's resident size stays on `Core\Os`, where a fact about the machine
belongs. The peak is recorded by the runtime as it happens, not on request, because Novis frees
memory promptly: a script that spent most of its life near the ceiling would otherwise report a
comfortable number at exit. Operators get the peak without any application code, in the exit
report, in a metric, and as a warning when a configured high-water mark is crossed.
